Build commands, test commands and project files

The published documentation uses Astro Starlight. It includes grouped navigation, page contents, full-text search, locally served fonts and a header text-size selector and resizable desktop navigation. See the website configuration.

Build it with npm ci and npm run build, then check it with npm run check:docs. The C99 benchmark itself needs only GCC and Make. Open dist/offline/index.html directly for the standalone offline reference.

The source review, before-and-after results, and heading review record the implementation and wording checks.

A standalone GCC/Make project comparing an exact-normalized baseline with twelve fuzzy algorithms. The checked-in report and CSVs come from actual execution. The program reruns correctness checks, calibrates only on development data, freezes the selected policies, evaluates held-out cases, and measures performance before writing a new report.

Build, test and run the C99 benchmark

Section titled “Build, test and run the C99 benchmark”

Only GCC, Make and the C standard library are needed. POSIX systems use clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC); other platforms use the isolated C99 clock() fallback. Run commands from this directory. No Python, C++, .NET or fuzzy-matching package is required. make benchmark and running the executable without arguments perform the default five-repetition experiment. The delivered report records seven repetitions.

make clean removes binaries and retains the datasets and evidence. The warning configuration is -std=c99 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wconversion -Wshadow. The sanitizer binary uses -g -O1 -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer. LeakSanitizer needs process access unavailable on the execution host and is disabled through its documented runtime hook. ASan and UBSan remain active. On an unrestricted host, rebuild with make -B SANITIZER_LEAKS=1 sanitize to enable leak checking too. The original host also reports that executable-name symbolization is unavailable; this does not disable address or UB detection.

Command-line options and dataset generation

Section titled “Command-line options and dataset generation”

The default seed is 42. Ordinary builds and benchmarks never regenerate data. An explicit regeneration changes the experiment and replaces both manifests:

The benchmark rejects a seed or version that disagrees with the manifest metadata. Costs are configurable nonnegative integers; repetitions range from 1 to 100. Numeric and unknown CLI arguments are validated. --report and --csv select primary output paths; create their parent directories first. Companion aggregate, runtime and calibration CSVs always go under reports/.

C99 modules and configuration binding

Section titled “C99 modules and configuration binding”

src/pm.h defines the shared API and bounded representations. src/parser.c handles entries; src/normalization.c handles ASCII normalization, tokens and schema collisions; src/configuration.c supplies data-driven typed registries and transactional binding; src/algorithms/ contains the twelve scorers; src/resolver.c provides exact-first matching, deterministic ranking and acceptance policy. Dataset generation/loading, calibration/evaluation, timing and reporting each have separate modules. tests/test_suite.c contains literal parser and binding cases, known-answer algorithm checks and an independent shortest-path edit-distance oracle.

bind_lines validates a batch without applying it. bind_configuration validates the entire batch and then stores raw strings plus typed integer/boolean values under canonical property indices. Failed validation leaves the supplied Configuration unchanged. Required-property and duplicate errors are explicit. Callers must keep inputs and registry immutable for the duration of binding. The example ten-line configuration is tested end to end.

Calibration and held-out test datasets

Section titled “Calibration and held-out test datasets”

The checked-in manifests contain 184 calibration and 380 held-out cases. The held-out category counts follow the requested distribution exactly. Calibration canonical vocabulary and family IDs are disjoint from evaluation. Cases include manually curated original examples and adversarial semantics plus deterministic xorshift32 mutations. Six data-driven schemas cover the original ten names, 30 adversarial names, twelve short names, 128-byte boundaries, a normalization collision and sixteen calibration names.

CSV columns are id,schema,category,input,expected,target,family. Expected labels are 0=resolved, 1=unknown, 2=ambiguous, 3=invalid input/schema. Input manifests intentionally use a simple unquoted CSV subset without commas/newlines in fields. The result CSV uses quoted and escaped text fields. In results.csv, expected_score=-1 means unavailable because the case has no intended target or the exact-only baseline has no fuzzy scorer; (none) marks an absent suggestion. Threshold fields for the exact baseline are ignored. All IDs and raw input/schema pairs are unique within a split. Loader and validation failures stop the run.

The unit suite covers parser boundaries, typed application, rollback, tokenization, numeric distinctions, collision handling, ambiguity, exact-match bypass and registry-order independence. An independent edit-graph oracle checks the distances. Compiler probes verify the bans in Git’s banned.h; see the standard-library review.

Generated reports and CSV files

Section titled “Generated reports and CSV files”
File Contents
reports/evaluation.md Measured report, category breakdowns, failures, calibration policies and recommendations
reports/results.csv Per-case outcomes, suggestions, intended/top scores, failure IDs and dangerous flags
reports/summary.csv Per-method confusion counts and selected thresholds
reports/runtime.csv Both measured paths at 10/50/100/1000 properties
reports/calibration_grid.csv Every calibration policy considered and its measured cost/coverage
reports/execution.log Delivered optimized execution transcript
reports/sanitizer.log Sanitized unit-suite execution
reports/sanitizer_full.log Sanitized complete experiment, excluded from comparative timing

Read algorithm definitions and methodology for formulas, policy interpretation, memory requirements and limitations. See the measured report for the actual recommendation. A small dangerous-error count still warrants attention: fuzzy matching does not establish the user’s intended meaning, and exact-only automatic binding with reviewed suggestions remains the conservative deployment option.

File articles and retained migrations

Section titled “File articles and retained migrations”

web/file-notes/ contains the explanations interleaved with exact code blocks on every source page. Headers live beside the C files in src/; src/pm.h enables the unmodified Git ban policy. Completed one-time editorial tools live under ad-hoc/. The repeatable build and check tools stay under scripts/.

Algorithm comments and worked calculations

Section titled “Algorithm comments and worked calculations”

Each algorithm file now names its intermediate costs and explains non-obvious storage or indexing. The file articles include small checked calculations beside the source and links to primary explanations. Learning references explains what to read in each source. AGENTS.md records commenting, reference and regression rules for future changes.

Refresh measured observations beside the code

Section titled “Refresh measured observations beside the code”

Run make feedback after a completed benchmark. It reads the recorded outcomes and timings, updates the marked observation comments and article sections, and leaves the worked calculations intact. Documentation preparation also refreshes those sections. Measured algorithm tradeoffs explains the observed differences and links real inputs to their outcomes.
